title: Guardrail self-tests and risk-map coverage
description: Gate scripts had no tests, so a checker bug would pass or block everything silently, and areas.tsv drifted when gate files were renamed or added. Add unittest suites for md_duplicates.py, docs_graph.py and no_comments.py, a test.sh check that every root file is explicitly mapped and every gate file rates high, and run both suites as pre-commit hooks so CI enforces them.
acceptance_criteria: Both suites pass in pre-commit --all-files; mutating each checker or dropping an areas.tsv rule makes a test fail.
notes:
probe
Review follow-ups merged too: coverage now checks by path, and any gates or ci row must rate high.
close_reason: Merged in PR #59 (e50871f): unittest suites for the 3 gate scripts plus risk-map coverage in test.sh, both running as pre-commit hooks in CI; mutation checks fail as expected.

title: Documentation ownership model and review checklist
description: Phase A step 1, first deliverable. One canonical definition per concept; ownership declaration per file; relative links to dependencies only; zero-duplication policy; ADRs explain why and link to current specifications without restating them; two A4 pages, ASCII diagrams, no version labels. Manual review checklist applies until Phase B automates it.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist exists and every later Phase A document is reviewed against it; ownership table maps each concept to exactly one file.
notes: Decided 2026-10-24: system ownership. Beads owns work items, dependencies, progress and execution order. Markdown owns requirements, architecture, invariants, contracts and design decisions. Executable guardrails own mechanical validation of documented policies. Impact recap owns what changed, why and the associated risk. A requirement or rule is maintained in exactly one of these; the others reference it.

title: Nonfunctional requirements
description: Avatar quality, conversation behavior (turn taking, interruption), latency budgets, privacy and egress targets, cost ceilings.
acceptance_criteria: Each target has an ID, a measurable threshold and a measurement method; no provider, model version or hardware is named as a requirement.

title: Business scenarios and acceptance criteria
description: User journeys and business scenarios for converse, recognize and act; Gate 1 and Gate 2 success criteria stated as observable outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Each scenario has an ID, actor, trigger, expected outcome and acceptance criteria; Gate 1 and Gate 2 criteria are measurable and reference scenario IDs.

title: Requirements and acceptance baseline
description: Phase A step 2. Business scenarios, acceptance criteria and nonfunctional requirements that the domain model, ports and slices derive from. Documentation only; no code.
acceptance_criteria: Requirements documents accepted under the documentation review checklist; every scenario and target has a stable ID that later documents reference; docs/README.md reading order places requirements between Engineering and Domain.
notes: Decided 2026-10-24: canonical owner is docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, read position 2 (after ENGINEERING.md, before DOMAIN.md). docs_graph.py accepts nested Markdown files, so a split past the size cap may use a folder; each part must be linked from docs/README.md and pass the existing size and graph rules.

title: Design consistency audit and freeze sign-off
description: Phase A step 8. Audit across requirements, domain, module graph, port catalog, slice execution graphs and traceability for duplicates, contradictions and uncovered behavior, then sign off. No code, gate or config file for the application lands before this closes.
acceptance_criteria: Five views consistent and complete: domain graph (rbp.1), module and dependency graph (rbp.2), contract graph (rbp.5), execution graph (rbp.3), validation traceability graph (rbp.12). Zero duplicate definitions and zero contradictions under the review checklist (3u0.3). Freeze scope per 3u0.2.
notes: Duplicate scanners (md_duplicates.py, jscpd) prove only textual uniqueness. The audit must also find competing definitions of one concept expressed in different words.

title: Settle the design-freeze decisions
description: Canonical ownership, enforcement scope, change discipline, gate semantics, session lifecycle ownership, failure vocabulary. Freeze scope rule: freeze domain boundaries, contracts, invariants, dependency directions and acceptance criteria; keep model versions, provider endpoints, runtime hardware and implementation-specific optimizations configurable.
notes: Decided 2026-10-24: (1) Comments ban stays strict. No explanatory comments in authored code; rationale lives in canonical Markdown and ADRs. Only machine-required exceptions: shebang on line 1, mandatory licence text, impact-recap PR markers. (2) Document links stay acyclic. Documents reference earlier authoritative definitions only; docs/README.md is the index; docs_graph.py enforces direction.
